A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRISM research work. All 24 pages of v3 and 23 pages of v4, including Appendices A–D, provide readable text, equations, figures and tables sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original PRISM experiments on Sudoku, OpenWebText, HumanEval and MBPP, plus calibration and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains original benchmark experiments and adds likelihood-learning comparisons, transfer results and coding error analyses.

M1.justification: The core scalar-quality PRISM method remains, but Appendix D.6 adds a substantial alternative: learning full conditional distributions with cross-entropy using the existing unmasking head, followed by entropy-adjusted remasking. V3's PRISM-loop terminal refinement procedure and Algorithm 4 are removed.

E1.justification: Both versions use Sudoku, OpenWebText, opc-sft-stage2 training data, and HumanEval/MBPP coding tasks. The new transfer, entropy and error analyses operate within this retained coverage; changed model configurations and decoding budgets do not introduce new datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: The established MDLM/MDM, ReMDM and ReMDM-conf baselines remain. V4 Table 3 adds likelihood-learning and entropy-aware likelihood variants as direct comparators to scalar PRISM, while the PRISM-loop comparison row disappears. Newly cited concurrent methods are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported OpenWebText fine-tuning configuration changes from k=8, n_y=4 to k=32, n_y=1. Its benchmark now reports PRISM at 64–1024 steps, replacing the broader PRISM/PRISM-loop evaluation spanning 16–4096 steps. New experiments introduce matched 10k-step versus 20k-step training comparisons and a separate PRISM corrector paired with an unfine-tuned LLaDA backbone.

E4.justification: V4 adds scalar-versus-likelihood training-budget comparisons, entropy/remasking diagnostics, a corrector-transfer experiment, syntax-error counts, and four coding success/failure case studies (Section 4.4; Appendices D.6–D.7). The earlier calibration and k/n_y/nucleus-sampling analyses are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The retained calibration practice is unchanged; new error counts and scatterplots do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: OpenWebText results are substantially revised: at 128 steps, PRISM's MAUVE/PPL/entropy changes from 0.175/17.9/5.10 to 0.278/23.9/5.32 under revised settings. ReMDM's 64-step MAUVE/PPL changes from 0.011/81.3 to 0.016/60.4. PRISM-loop and several decoding-budget entries disappear. New results include likelihood variants, 19 of 26 syntax errors reportedly corrected, and a separate transfer comparison of 23.2% versus 34.1%. Sudoku and the main coding benchmark results are retained.

T1.justification: The masking-equivalence proof and scalar/multi-token PRISM guarantees are retained with renumbering. Appendix D.6 adds a cross-entropy objective with a claimed conditional-likelihood minimizer and formally defines an entropy-adjusted quality score. It supplies no substantial new proof.

C1.justification: The central claims of lightweight, theoretically grounded self-correction across domains remain. V4's introduction explicitly extends the coding-performance claim to HumanEval, whose results already appeared in v3. Its conclusion adds an explicit priority claim that earlier work does not target per-token quality through an efficient training objective.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive interpretations of corrector transferability, scalar-versus-distribution training efficiency, and entropy-aware remasking. New failure cases identify overcorrection and illustrate global structural errors. Appendix D.6 warns that remasking valid high-entropy tokens can be harmful, although Section 3 retains v3's conflicting statement that this cannot hurt.

D1.justification: V4 adds a code-release link in the abstract and explicitly documents confidence-based subset selection for the main OpenWebText training, versus random selection in the retained ablations. It also documents the new variants' training budgets and removes PRISM-loop implementation details. Most hardware, optimizer, LoRA and data-processing information is retained.

R1.justification: A new concurrent-work paragraph adds Meshchaninov, Li and Huang et al. (2025), and Schiff and Bie et al. (2026), discussing their relationship to PRISM's inputs and scalar-quality learning. The earlier related-work taxonomy and most references remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing exposition and section ordering remain. V4 integrates the former 'Why self-correction?' passage into the introduction, moves calibration discussion into a new mechanistic-analysis subsection, streamlines Algorithm 1, revises the conclusion and removes the contents page. These are localized editorial changes alongside the scientific additions.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. V4 redraws and consolidates the overview/training diagrams, merges the coding tables, restructures the OpenWebText table and plot, and adds likelihood-comparison, entropy-diagnostic and code-example displays. Existing ablation and calibration figures are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The controlled scalar-versus-likelihood comparison, explicit failure analyses and code-access information strengthen empirical support and transparency. The net gain is limited: v4 removes the 4096-step comparison showing ReMDM's MAUVE advantage, leaves conflicting statements about harmless remasking, and Table 4's claimed syntax correction still displays invalid code ('if bracket == <:'). The core proofs and coding scores remain unchanged.
